results.title: Flooding from rivers and sea
results.summary: This spot is on, or within about 5 m of, a High rivers and sea zone.
results.what_this_means: These zones show the chance of flooding from rivers or the sea in any one year, allowing for flood defences, which reduce the risk but don't remove it. High is 1 in 30 or more, Medium is between 1 in 30 and 1 in 100, Low is between 1 in 100 and 1 in 1,000, and Very Low is below 1 in 1,000. Being near a zone doesn't mean this home would flood.
results.how_sure: The Environment Agency says this data estimates risk to an area of land and is generally not suitable for assessing one property. Our distances can read up to about 6 m too close, and on a zone means on it or within about 5 m.
what_you_can_do: Check the official Environment Agency map for this address.
Sign up for free flood warnings if you're near a zone.
Ask your insurer or a surveyor about this particular home before making a decision.

results.title: Flooding from surface water
results.summary: The nearest mapped surface water zone is Low, about 40 m away.
results.what_this_means: These zones show where rainwater may lie or flow when it can't drain away, and the chance of that in any one year. High is 1 in 30 or more, Medium is between 1 in 30 and 1 in 100, and Low is between 1 in 100 and 1 in 1,000. The Environment Agency treats anywhere outside these zones as Very Low, not as no risk. Being near a zone doesn't mean this home would flood.
results.how_sure: The Environment Agency says this data estimates risk to an area of land and is generally not suitable for assessing one property. Our distances can read up to about 6 m too close, and on a zone means on it or within about 5 m.

results.title: Clay subsidence
results.summary: Much of London sits on clay that can shrink and swell. We can't assess this particular home.
results.what_this_means: Clay soils shrink as they dry and swell as they get wet, and this movement can damage foundations and walls. In the British Geological Survey's national summary, about 86% of London's area falls in its Significant class. That figure is PerilMap's own calculation from this data.
results.how_sure: This is general information for London, not a result for this location. The British Geological Survey marks this data as not suitable for local or site specific analysis.
what_you_can_do: If you're buying, ask your surveyor about ground conditions and any signs of movement.
Consider a detailed report for this address from the British Geological Survey.
If you notice new or growing cracks, speak to a surveyor or your insurer.
